result.question: Why did Zebul send messengers?

readings.answer: To inform Abimelech that Gaal and his brothers were stirring up the city against him.
readings.support: Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you.

readings.answer: To urge Abimelech to come by night, lie in wait, and then advance against the city.
readings.support: Now then, tonight you and the people with you are to come and lie in wait in the fields. | And in the morning at sunrise, get up and advance against the city.

assessments.reason: The text states the messengers told Abimelech, “Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you,” which is a direct warning about Gaal.

The message also includes tactical urging—“tonight you… lie in wait… in the morning… advance against the city”—so giving instructions is another stated purpose, though it is different from the key’s emphasis on warning.
